stories.title: S&P 500 adds little-known industrial stock in latest index reshuffle
stories.summary: The S&P 500 is making a change to its roster, adding a relatively obscure industrial company. The move comes as the index itself sits at what CNBC describes as a key 'battleground level,' with some pointing to a lesser-followed index as a possible signal for where the market goes next.
stories.whyItMatters: Index additions can drive forced buying from funds that track the S&P 500, and the broader index's stall at a technical level matters for anyone gauging market direction.
whatToWatch: Whether the new addition sees a bump from index-fund buying
How the S&P 500 resolves its standoff at the cited battleground level
questions: Which obscure index is being used as the tell, and why?
How much passive-fund flow will the new addition attract?

stories.title: S&P 500 posts first July decline since 2014
stories.summary: The S&P 500 closed out July with a loss, marking the index's first negative July since 2014. MarketWatch identifies specific stocks that led the pullback during the month.
stories.whyItMatters: A rare seasonal decline breaks a long streak of July strength and raises questions about whether momentum is fading heading into the back half of the year.
whatToWatch: August trading to see if the selloff extends or reverses
Performance of the specific laggard stocks named in the selloff
questions: Was the decline driven by broad rotation or a handful of large-cap losers?

stories.title: Investors eye front end of yield curve ahead of next Fed meetings
stories.summary: CNBC reports that Wall Street strategists are advising investors to focus on the front end of the yield curve as the market anticipates the Federal Reserve's upcoming policy meetings.
stories.whyItMatters: Short-term rates are the most sensitive to Fed policy expectations, making the front end a key barometer for how markets are pricing future rate decisions.
whatToWatch: Movements in short-dated Treasury yields ahead of the next Fed meeting
Fed communications between now and the next policy decision
questions: How many rate moves are currently priced into the front end?

stories.title: Stocks end July on hopeful note after historic momentum-trade unwind
stories.summary: July closed with a more optimistic tone for stocks even after the momentum trade suffered its biggest wipeout since 2000, according to MarketWatch. The rebound suggests some stabilization after a rough stretch for high-momentum names.
stories.whyItMatters: A momentum unwind of this magnitude can ripple through popular trading strategies and funds, so its aftermath is closely watched for signs of broader market stress or recovery.
whatToWatch: Whether momentum stocks continue to stabilize into August
Fund flows into and out of momentum-based strategies
questions: What specifically triggered the momentum unwind?

stories.title: Fed proposes modernizing rules for mutual banking organizations and insider lending
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve Board requested public comment on two proposals: one to modernize rules for mutual banking organizations, and another to update its rule on extending credit to bank 'insiders' such as executives, board members, and major shareholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to insider-lending and mutual bank rules affect governance and risk controls at banks, which matters for financial-sector investors and regulators alike.
whatToWatch: Length and outcome of the public comment period
Final rule language once adopted
questions: How significantly would the proposed changes alter current insider-lending limits?

stories.title: Analysis: Markets read Warsh as dovish, but his own words hint at a hike
stories.summary: CNBC analysis argues that while markets have interpreted Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's recent comments as dovish, a closer look at his own statements suggests he may be leaning toward a rate hike.
stories.whyItMatters: A gap between market perception and the Fed chair's actual signals raises the risk of a surprise policy move that could jolt rate-sensitive assets.
whatToWatch: Upcoming Fed communications for clarification on Warsh's stance
Market repricing if a hike appears more likely
questions: Is the market misreading Warsh's language, or is the analysis overreading it?

stories.title: Inflation indicators sit near multi-year lows as Warsh's Fed faces pressure to act
stories.summary: CNBC reports that several inflation indicators are at their lowest levels in years even as Kevin Warsh's Federal Reserve faces pressure to take action on inflation.
stories.whyItMatters: The disconnect between falling inflation gauges and calls for Fed action highlights the uncertainty facing markets over the central bank's next move.
whatToWatch: Upcoming inflation data releases
Fed statements addressing the pressure to act
questions: Which specific indicators are being cited as at multi-year lows?
What is driving the pressure to act despite low readings?

stories.summary: CNBC reports that Federal Reserve officials who voted for a rate hike are publicly stating that immediate action is needed to combat inflation.
stories.whyItMatters: Public dissent or urgency from voting Fed officials signals potential division on the committee, which markets watch closely for clues on the path of rates.

The next scheduled FOMC decision

stories.title: Eaton shares jump on earnings, outlook seen as sign of AI buildout resilience
stories.summary: Shares of Eaton rose after the company's earnings and forward guidance suggested continued strength in demand tied to the AI infrastructure buildout, according to CNBC.
stories.whyItMatters: Eaton's results are being read as a bellwether for industrial and electrical-equipment demand linked to AI data center growth, a theme investors are tracking closely.

stories.title: New York sues Kalshi over prediction-market operations
stories.summary: New York has filed suit against prediction-market platform Kalshi, alleging it is running an 'illegal gambling operation,' according to CNBC.
stories.whyItMatters: The lawsuit adds to regulatory pressure on prediction markets, a fast-growing corner of financial and event-contract trading that has drawn scrutiny from multiple state and federal regulators.

Whether other states follow with similar actions
questions: How does this suit interact with Kalshi's existing federal regulatory status?
